overview: Despatch describes Domei's 1938 Hong Kong office, run by Horiguchi with few local clients, judged a propaganda tool amid rumors the Hong Kong Press took German and Japanese subsidies.

people.name: Robert Y. Horiguchi
people.role: Manager of the Domei News Agency office in Hong Kong; formerly a journalism student at the University of Missouri and an employee of the Hearst International News Service in Chicago

people.name: Addison E. Southard
people.role: American Consul General in Hong Kong

subfiles.title: Despatch on the opening of the Domei News Agency office in Hong Kong
subfiles.from: Addison E. Southard, American Consul General in Hong Kong
subfiles.about: Reports on the establishment, personnel, customers, and apparent propaganda purpose of the Domei News Agency’s new Hong Kong office.
subfiles.summary: Southard reports Domei's unprofitable 1938 Hong Kong office spread pro-Japanese war news, amid rumors the Hong Kong Press took German and Japanese money.

interest: Shows Domei's 1938 Hong Kong news office as a propaganda venture rather than a commercial one, amid German-subsidy rumors.
